source.title: BLADE: Bilevel Low-rank Augmented-Lagrangian Erasure for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Md Toufikuzzaman; Ahmad Mousavi; Dongwon Lee

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether attacks recover knowledge after unlearning, using BLADE and other methods rather than reproducing one of the named original methods.
record.gate_note: The paper directly evaluates paraphrased and perturbed extraction, jailbreak prompts, GCG suffixes, and fine-tuning on the forget set. It also reports ordinary forgetting and retention metrics for BLADE. The membership-inference results concern membership leakage rather than recovery of targeted knowledge and are not recorded as rows. No activation-direction ablation or quantization attack is reported. Table 14's detailed extraction values are flattened in the supplied text; the paper's explicit summary of BLADE's extraction-attack ranking is recorded instead.
record.test_reason: BLADE is a new unlearning method, not an original source. The authors run their own black-box attacks on it: paraphrase/perturbation extraction, two jailbreak templates and GCG suffixes. They also run a relearning attack, fine-tuning on the forget set. They report forgetting and retention against a gold retrained model. These results bear on A, E and F, and loosely on B.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude BLADE beats baselines on TOFU, MUSE and KnowUndo composites and stays stable under 4× scaling and sequential unlearning. They say it resists black-box extraction, jailbreak, MIA and GCG attacks. They concede it is susceptible to relearning attacks, attributing this to the lack of an adversarial safety margin.
record.recipe_differences: BLADE is a new constrained bilevel method using LoRA, retain repair, an asymmetric augmented Lagrangian, and clamped entropy; it is not a reproduction of the original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack outcome varies with attack type and TOFU forget split; BLADE's MUSE News forgetting is weaker than its MUSE Books result. The relearning result is single-seed.

fits_no_version.finding: MIA PrivLeak: BLADE 88.4/50.5/56.5, positive, with most baselines negative (Table 16).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods differ in membership-inference leakage on the forget set.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The relearning attack is reported at limited scale with a single seed and as a composite HM decrease rather than direct recovery accuracy. The supplied Table 14 extraction results are flattened, and no never-trained comparison is reported for the prompt attacks. MUSE News has much higher measured forget-knowledge accuracy than MUSE Books. No quantization or activation-direction attack is tested.
record.rows_left_out: No per-method membership-inference rows were extracted because PrivLeak measures membership leakage, not recovery of the targeted knowledge. Detailed Table 14 attack values were not assigned to individual splits because the supplied text flattens the table; its explicit BLADE ranking summary is recorded in r13.

untested.parts: Hazardous-knowledge (WMDP-style) targets and broad general-ability benchmarks on TOFU/MUSE; never-trained comparison for attacks.
Relearning on unrelated, loosely related, or held-out subsets of forgotten facts; per-setting recovery accuracy.
Entire version: no activation-direction ablation or blocking-vs-deletion analysis.
Other languages and in-context information; attacks only on TOFU 1B (jailbreak/GCG).
Resistance to activation edits and quantization.

missing.what: LLM-judge forget leakage on TOFU 3B: BLADE FL 0.010/0.023/0.034 on a 0–2 scale.
KnowUndo BLADE: copyright fgt_R .040 vs FT .244; privacy fgt_R .128 vs FT .665. Text says recall is cut 81% with 87% of retain quality kept.
Jailbreak and GCG values for baseline methods (e.g. SimNPO jailbreak ASR .50–.55), usable as E evidence for other methods.
Adversarial extraction Adv_HM per split for 1B and 3B.

record.verdict_notes: The relearning attack trains on the very facts evaluated, without a retrained-model control, so it only weakly bears on B's hidden-knowledge claim. Attack results use only TOFU, mostly the 1B model. The gold retrained model's scores serve as the practical chance baseline for forgetting rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare attack recovery with an untrained model that never saw the target knowledge; the reported extraction composite is not a direct recovery rate.
Tests fine-tuning on the original forget set, not unrelated or loosely related examples; reports an average composite-score change rather than separate direct recovery rates for each model and split.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking access versus deleting knowledge.
Tests paraphrased/perturbed queries, two jailbreak templates, and GCG suffixes on TOFU; no other languages or in-context information.
Tests resistance to the reported black-box attacks and a forget-set relearning attack; no resistance test for activation edits or quantization.
